hook.text: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98.7% of their DNA. The remaining 1.3% built two very different species.

buildup.text: Molecular clocks estimate the split at roughly 6–7 million years ago—matching the oldest hominin fossils.

discovery.text: The divergence wasn't instant. Gene flow may have continued for a million years after the initial split.

twist.text: Some genes diverged 10 million years ago; others only 4 million—speciation was messy and gradual.

climax.text: We didn't split cleanly from chimps. We slowly unstuck, like pulling apart two pieces of warm taffy.

punchline.text: Becoming separate species took millions of years.

quiz.question: How much DNA do humans and chimpanzees share?
